clue.text: Gamble on this and more in debt — a disaster!

indicators.note: a disaster is a wreck, so the letters before it are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the last letter in the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: A warning that betting more and sinking deeper into debt will end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a disaster' does double duty in the surface but only 'disaster' signals the shuffle; the A beside it joins AND MORE IN DEBT to make the fourteen letters. The answer is a slot machine with a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine with a single lever is where a gambler stakes coins, so it is the thing one gambles on.

clue.text: 5 dismissed decree

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a decree is a law handed down

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference '5', the answer to 5 Across, BANDIT. A cricketer who is dismissed is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living beyond the protection and rules of society, which is a fugitive criminal.

clue.text: Priest gets 26 right with a panacea

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
the answer to 26 Across is ELEVEN, written XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A clergyman picks up a team of eleven and the right cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' points to the answer of 26 Across, ELEVEN, which is used here as the Roman numeral XI.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all potion of alchemy, the supposed remedy for every ill, is exactly what a panacea is.

clue.text: Account about wine

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word for concerning or about
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A write-up on the subject of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a written or spoken description of events, a statement of what happened.

clue.text: Once place for commentary

parts.note: ex means former, what something once was
a place and a position are both a spot or location

explanation.surface: A spot where remarks used to be made.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed explanation or interpretation of a text is both a commentary and an expository account.

clue.text: See 1
A quiet father that's obvious

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a father is one kind of parent

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken dad whose nature is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain to see and evident to all is apparent, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Fellow, a conservative, is the recipient

parts.note: a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A college fellow who votes Tory turns out to be the beneficiary.
explanation.walkthrough: A DON is a university teacher; TORY is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom a gift or donation is made is the recipient of it, a legal term for a grantee.

clue.text: Maybe tether and cut to intimidate

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters might be arranged some other way, so they are shuffled
cut tells us to chop the last letter off the word and

explanation.surface: Tying up an animal and slashing it as a way to frighten someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the D from AND to leave AN; 'Maybe' then rearranges TETHER with AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone with harm is to intimidate them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Follow tube to suction part of pump

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them closely
a pipe is a tube

explanation.surface: Instructions for tracing a tube to the sucking end of a pump.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipe through which a pump draws in fluid at its lower end is called the tailpipe in pump engineering.

clue.text: Cricketer candid with Queen

parts.note: candid and open both mean frank and honest
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A sportsman speaking frankly with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an opener is one of the two batsmen who start the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who begins the innings for his side is a type of cricketer.

clue.text: Be declared keeper

parts.note: 'Be' spoken sounds like the insect bee, so the clue reads as a keeper of bees

explanation.walkthrough: 'declared' means said out loud: 'Be' sounds like 'bee', so a 'bee keeper' is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps hives of honey-making insects is an apiarist, from Latin apis.

clue.text: Shrub a toper cultivates

indicators.note: to cultivate is to work over the ground, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker turns gardener and grows a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: A toper is a heavy drinker; 'cultivates' rearranges A TOPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African flowering bush with large showy heads is a protea, so the answer is a kind of shrub.

clue.text: Dare Frank and I disturb beef cattle?

indicators.note: to disturb something is to throw it into disorder, so the named letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A challenge to two people to go and upset some cows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturb' rearranges DARE, FRANK and I; 'and' is only a link joining the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African breed of cattle kept for meat is the Afrikander, so the answer names beef stock.

clue.text: Employees tend to notice hospital worker

parts.note: the employees of an organisation are its staff
to tend to a patient is to nurse them

explanation.surface: Workers look after the sick and pay attention to a ward employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' is a link here, carrying no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualified nurse on a ward, ranked below a sister, works in a hospital.

clue.text: Before noon I send message — to be friendly

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, means before noon
to cable is to send a message by telegraph

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to send a cordial telegram first thing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Being friendly and good-natured toward others is being amicable, from Latin amicus, friend.

clue.text: Yet time for a frame

parts.note: yet and still both mean even now
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Still not the moment for framing a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand or raised support for barrels or goods is a stillage, a kind of frame or stand.

clue.text: New moon — note change but sameness in colour

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the letters into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Observing the new moon prompts a remark about a dull colour palette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' joins the surface and is a link; 'change' rearranges MOON and NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A single shade throughout, without variety, describes a monotone colour scheme.

clue.text: Slip to Rome in disguise there's a city!

indicators.note: disguised letters keep their identity but change their look, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sneak off to Rome incognito: what a city!
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a large and important city, a chief urban centre.

clue.text: Wager not well inside sol' quarters!

indicators.note: inside places the word for poorly within the word for a stake

parts.note: a wager is a bet
to be not well is to be ill

explanation.surface: A sick soldier puts a bet on in the barracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging assigned to troops in a private house is a billet, where soldiers are quartered.

clue.text: Rigid leading performer joins companion

parts.note: a star is the leading performer in a show
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A stiff headline actor teams up with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour. 'Rigid' is an adjective, used as a noun-like stiffness: starch stands for formality and stiffness.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is the stiffening agent for collars, and figuratively stiff formality, so it stands for rigidity.

clue.text: Make mistake with worker by wandering

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone blunders while a labourer drifts about.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant describes roaming in search of adventure, as a knight errant does, so it means straying.

clue.text: Inexperienced airman returns depressed

indicators.note: returns means the abbreviation for the airman is read backwards

parts.note: LAC is a leading aircraftman in the RAF
depressed means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A raw young pilot comes back feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow describes youthful immaturity, lacking the experience of the world.

clue.text: I tar road perhaps and feel heat from it

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters could be put together differently, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road worker spreading hot tar feels the warmth coming off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges I TAR ROAD; the definition is a description of a heater, the thing you feel warmth from.
explanation.definitionFit: A heating appliance that gives off warmth into a room is something you feel the heat from.

clue.text: Lighthouse could be a trick

parts.note: could be gives the verb be
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A suspicion that a lighthouse may be a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire or light guiding ships, the job of a lighthouse.

clue.text: Feldspar could provide aural aid

indicators.note: could provide suggests the letters can be made into something else when reworked

explanation.surface: A mineral that might serve as a hearing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Adularia is a translucent variety of the mineral orthoclase, a potassium feldspar such as moonstone.

clue.text: Not odd to follow the Spanish team

indicators.note: to follow places the word for not odd after the Spanish article

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a number that is not odd is even

explanation.surface: Fans of a Spanish side insist it is not odd to follow them.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side of that many players is commonly called an eleven.

clue.text: Swing torch in church-time for musical note

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: to swing a torch is to wave it about, so its letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Waving a torch during church services is the cue for a note of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swing' rearranges TORCH into ROTCH, which 'in' puts inside CE (Church of England), followed by T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a quarter note in music, one beat in common time.
